findings.section: Behaviour contract U1 / Worked example / Acceptance
findings.summary: The reported pre-fix output-reading and output-writing failure is not reproducible through the gate runner under the brief's stated Windows code-page-437 condition.
findings.evidence: The brief says at lines 106-119 that redirected state.RunGate starts with 437 for both console encodings, and at lines 128-133 and 194-195 that the cafe read and Write-Output assertions fail on the base. On Windows with chcp reporting 437 and unmodified internal/state/gate.go, an in-module probe using state.RunGate against pwsh 7.7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1 produced, respectively, `65001, 437, 65001` and `65001, 437, 20127` for Output/Input/$OutputEncoding. A temporary git commit whose subject was cafe passed the Select-String gate in both shells, and both emitted cafe as `63 61 66 c3 a9 0d 0a`. Thus T1 and T2 pass before the fix in the acceptance environment; the report's broader encoding-state assertion is what fails there, not the two native-output claims.
findings.fix: Correct the defect table, pre-fix worked-example result, and acceptance proof to match redirected-gate behaviour. Base the failing assertion on the observed unsatisfied InputEncoding/$OutputEncoding contract (and the Windows PowerShell 5.1 stdin case), and describe the native-read/write cases as regression coverage unless a separate, reproducible launch condition actually makes them fail.

decisions: vloop itself sets PowerShell encodings inside the process rather than relying on profiles or machine settings; this is appropriate for deterministic repository commands.
The setting applies on every OS; I agree because it keeps one invocation path and one cross-platform contract.
The contract sets Console.OutputEncoding, Console.InputEncoding and $OutputEncoding to BOM-less UTF-8; this covers native stdout, console input and native stdin respectively.
The setup mechanism is left to the implementer, provided the command remains operational after an encoding setter failure.
The operator chose `cafe` as the literal fixture; it is a suitable one-code-point non-ASCII case, though the brief should pin the byte and newline expectations as it currently does.
